facts.text: A covered provider sent a PHI-bearing treatment message. The verified intended recipient was the treating clinic, but the verified actual destination was a different, unrelated recipient.
The operator says a separate authorization might permit sending to the actual recipient.
Whether any separate permission applies to the actual recipient has not been established.

required_questions.question: Assess the observed recipient and stated purpose; distinguish incident evidence from an unverified separate basis.

facts.text: The sender is a covered provider. A PHI-bearing referral is intended for a verified treating provider for treatment of the individual. The configured recipient exactly matches that verified treating provider.

The message contains ordinary referral data, not psychotherapy notes or substance-use-disorder records. No sale, marketing, agreed restriction, conflicting notice or other special prohibition applies in the supplied scenario.
Names and full service dates remain in the treatment referral. De-identification is not the asserted disclosure basis.

required_questions.question: Check this stated treatment recipient/purpose only; do not turn it into an analytics de-identification requirement.

facts.text: A covered provider plans an analytics export using Safe Harbor as its sole approved release path for this export.
The export retains medical record numbers and full individual admission dates. No actual patient values are supplied in this synthetic test.

The scenario explicitly establishes that no expert determination was performed. No other release path has been approved for this export; this is an affirmative scenario fact, not an inference from a missing document.

This synthetic organization's approved export plan requires successful Safe Harbor verification before this specific export. This is a local prerequisite, not a claim that HIPAA has only one release path.

required_questions.question: Check the explicitly selected release path against the observed data and distinguish local release failure from definitive illegality.

facts.text: For this analytics export a person with appropriate statistical and scientific knowledge and experience applied generally accepted methods, determined a very small identification risk for the anticipated recipient using reasonably available information, and documented the methods and result.

The documented expert determination covers this exact data and anticipated recipient, including the retained full dates. Safe Harbor is not the selected path. No contrary identification evidence is supplied.
The operator's separate explanation is that encrypting the file automatically makes it de-identified. This explanation is not the documented expert's reasoning.

required_questions.question: Assess the established release path without substituting an operator's unsupported rationale or Safe Harbor for the documented expert determination.

facts.text: A covered provider configured a future analytics export described as de-identified. No actual export or delivery has occurred.
The operator says the data will satisfy Safe Harbor, but that assertion has not been verified.
The actual output fields and identifier-removal checks are unknown. No expert-determination facts are supplied; their absence here does not establish that no determination exists.

required_questions.question: Identify the verification gap without converting missing information into an affirmative failed condition.

facts.text: An isolated synthetic system reported a ransomware alert and service disruption. This packet supplies no disclosure, recipient, export or de-identification scenario.
The cause, scope, PHI access and any notification duties have not been investigated. Security-incident and breach analysis is outside this narrow evidence template.

required_questions.question: Record the unsupported issue for human investigation rather than manufacturing a disclosure or breach conclusion.
